Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are Templeton's redlines to the MSA + Order Form with a focus on output ownership and any rights to use customer data/outputs for training or product improvements. High level asks from our side:

- Templeton needs to retain ownership of all outputs generated by our users (including derivatives) for product integration and compliance reasons.
- Templeton will not agree to any clause that allows Redwood to train models on raw customer content. We can consider a narrow, de-identified telemetry/operational feedback agreement but want it explicitly constrained.
- Please flag any MFN/reciprocity language and any broad ‘‘feedback’’ or ‘‘improvement’’ licenses — we want tight limits and a clear opt-out path.

Attached: Templeton_redlines_v3.pdf (redlines + cover note). Can you confirm Redwood's negotiable positions and whether legal can provide suggested counter-language? If possible, we’d like a short call next week to finalize the Order Form so procurement can move to signatures.

Subject: Re: Templeton redlines — suggested counter-language + options

Sofia and team — reviewed the redlines. I put together three pragmatic options (quick summary below) and attached a doc with proposed redline text (RI_proposed_clauses_v2.docx).

Option A (Customer-first — strict):
- Templeton owns all Outputs and Derivative Works.
- Redwood will not use any Customer Content or Outputs for model training or to improve models. Redwood may retain telemetry for billing/ops (no model training).
- Risk: limits product improvement; higher cost to Redwood.

Option B (Operational telemetry — recommended):
- Templeton owns all Outputs and Derivative Works.
- Redwood may collect limited, aggregated, and de-identified telemetry for model performance, latency, and regression detection, explicitly excluding any raw content or user output that could be reconstructed. Clause: Redwood receives a non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable license to use aggregated and de-identified feedback solely to maintain and operate the Service; such data will not be used to train foundation models.
- Includes opt-out: Templeton may request exclusion of specific workspaces/keys.
- Benefit: balances Templeton's IP protections with our ability to maintain quality.

Option C (Broader feedback license):
- Templeton grants Redwood a limited right to use Feedback (as defined) to improve models and services; strong anonymization and legal safeguards.
- Risk: likely a blocker for Templeton procurement.

Recommendation: Offer Option B as our default commercial compromise, with Option A as an escalated concession (in exchange for higher fees or reserved capacity commitments). I annotated a set of short paragraph counters in the attached.

If all agree, I’ll circulate the redline (doc attached) and propose a 30-minute call with Templeton legal to walk options.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ownership pathways & feedback license — our proposed compromise

Hi Elise / James — thanks for sending the redlines. Based on internal counsel's review, we propose Option B (Operational telemetry) as the middle ground:

- Templeton retains ownership of all Outputs and Derivative Works.
- Redwood is permitted to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and feedback strictly for service maintenance, regressions, and ops; not for training foundation models.
- We’ll include an exclusion mechanism for sensitive workspaces or API keys at Templeton's request.

Commercial note: we can accept Option B at the standard enterprise rate; if Templeton requires Option A (no telemetry at all), we would need to discuss a premium for a training-exclusion addendum (or minimum committed spend).

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to lock language? I can do 10:00–12:00 ET.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
